But they pushed forward and showed that good things can come out of the countryside,” said Bartley, who is also deputy mayor of Falmouth. He added that the athletes had demonstrated that young people could excel both academically and on the field, providing positive examples for others in Wakefield and across the parish. Bartley also praised the trio for the pride they had brought to Trelawny, noting that their achievements reflected well on the community and the wider parish. “I really like how all of them big up Trelawny and how they make Trelawny look good. They are from Wakefield; they are from the parish,” he said. He encouraged the young athletes to draw inspiration from Jamaica’s sprinting greats Usain Bolt and Veronica Campbell-Brown as they continue to develop their careers and pursue further success on the international stage. The three were recognised by the Trelawny Municipal Corporation (TMC) for their achievements at the national and international levels, as well as their leadership and positive influence on young people. Matheson, a student of William Knibb Memorial High School and former student of Wakefield Primary School, has distinguished himself in the 200-metre and 400-metre events. He captained William Knibb’s track and field team to victory in the 4x400-metre relay at Western Championships, where the team broke the existing record. The team also secured a top-10 finish in the 4x100-metre relay at the national championships. Matheson further demonstrated his potential in Canada, where he broke the Under-20 200-metre record and earned medals in both sprint events. Seymour, a former William Knibb student, enjoyed an impressive 2026 season, winning the Under-20 200-metre gold medal at the Carifta Games in Grenada before successfully defending his Class One 100-metre and 200-metre titles at the ISSA/GraceKennedy Boys’ and Girls’ Athletics Championships. He also won the Class One 100-metre event at Western Championships. His international campaign culminated in a bronze medal as a member of Jamaica’s men’s 4x100-metre relay team at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships. Seymour has also excelled academically, earning six Caribbean Secondary Education Certificate subjects. He received the award for the sportsperson with the best academic results at graduation, along with the prestigious William Knibb Ambassador Award. Dixon, meanwhile, has established herself as another promising talent from Wakefield. A Western Championships record holder, she has represented Jamaica at the Under-17 and Under-20 levels in the 400 metres and 4x400-metre relay. In July 2026, she finished third in the 400 metres while representing Jamaica in Mexico. She later clocked a personal-best 52.64 seconds at the Jamaica Under-20 trials in Kingston before advancing to the semi-finals of the 400 metres at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships, where she finished fifth in her semi-final. Now a scholarship recipient at Holmwood Technical High School, Dixon continues to balance her academic and athletic pursuits while contributing to community sporting activities and encouraging her peers. Wakefield has also produced other notable track and field talents, including Shanoya Douglas, further underscoring the community’s contribution to Jamaica’s rich athletics tradition. She was also awarded by the TMC in a recent civic ceremony. The recognition of Matheson, Seymour and Dixon highlights Wakefield’s contribution to Jamaica’s track and field talent pool and the promise of a new generation aspiring to represent the country with distinction. headline: Japan To Allow Sale Of Emergency Contraception Pills Without Prescription - BW Healthcare World
snippet: In a big step towards joining dozens of other nations that currently allow such sales at pharmacies, Japan's health ministry announced Monday that it will allow the trial sale of emergency contraceptives without a prescription beginning this summer, Kyodo News reported. A ministry panel has approved the sale of so called morning after pills at pharmacies that have trained pharmacists, private rooms, and are available on weekends, nights and holidays through March. They must also be able to coordinate with obstetrics and gynaecology clinics in the area. As per the current rules, women, even sexual assault victims, have to travel to a clinic or hospital for a prescription to purchase emergency contraception, which works best within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse, as per Kyodo News. Kyodo News is a Japan-based news agency established in November 1945. A ministry panel debated selling the medicine without a prescription in 2017, but the ministry stopped short of giving the green light, with critics claiming that making a morning-after pill available would encourage irresponsible use of the drug after intercourse. According to research conducted by the Health, Labour, and Welfare Ministry, emergency contraception has been available without a prescription in around 90 countries, according to Kyodo News. Clinical research done both at home and abroad show that emergency contraceptive tablets have an 80 per cent efficacy rate. Medical professionals have urged for increased access to the medicine in Japan, arguing that it might give rape victims a vital recourse while potentially lowering the need for abortions. Following the Cabinet's approval of various gender equality policies in late 2020, debates related to the over-the-counter distribution of emergency contraception pills have resumed. From the end of December to the beginning of January, the health ministry received 46,312 public comments, with the vast majority in favour of the trial sale, Kyodo News reported. (ANI)

headline: Trump Administration Invokes Defense Production Act for $150M Fuel Production
snippet: The Trump administration announced Thursday that it will invoke the Defense Production Act to allocate $150 million toward increasing U. S. production of gasoline and diesel. The Department of Energy stated in a press release that this funding is intended to boost refining output by millions of gallons per day, aiming to lower fuel costs for Americans who have been paying an average of more than $4 per gallon over the past three months. However, energy experts and industry representatives indicated that this measure is unlikely to provide short-term relief for household budgets. Patrick De Haan, a petroleum expert at GasBuddy, told CBS News that the initiative is "not going to have any impact" because global market forces, rather than domestic supply shortages, are driving current price levels. He noted that disruptions from the Iran conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war have pushed crude oil prices to their highest levels since May, with Brent crude reaching $116 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate trading around $103 a barrel as of Friday. Domestic Production Exceeds Consumption The core issue identified by industry analysts is that the United States already produces more fuel than it consumes domestically. Data cited by experts shows that the U. S. produces approximately 9.5 million barrels of gasoline per day, while domestic consumption sits at 8.9 million barrels. Similarly, production of distillate fuel oil, which includes diesel, stands at around 5.3 million barrels per day against a consumption rate of 3.6 million barrels. Tom Kloza, chief energy adviser for Gulf Oil, explained that because the U. S. exports about 1.4 million barrels of diesel daily, there is "no slack in U. S. refining." Consequently, political directives cannot immediately expand physical production capacity beyond current operational limits.

headline: UAE sets four levels for calculating private sector end-of-service gratuity
snippet: Abu Dhabi: The UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation has set out four levels for calculating end-of-service gratuity for foreign workers in the private sector: fractions of a year, the first period, years of service and the maximum gratuity. The ministry said the gratuity is calculated at 21 days’ wages for each of the first five years of service and 30 days’ wages for each additional year. Workers are also entitled to gratuity for fractions of a year in proportion to the period worked, provided they have completed one continuous year of service. The total end-of-service gratuity must not exceed two years’ wages, in accordance with applicable regulations. The ministry explained through its social media accounts that employers are required to pay end-of-service benefits and any wages due to workers within 14 days of the termination of their contracts. It also highlighted an optional alternative system for end-of-service benefits, known as the savings system, which allows end-of-service benefits to be invested and grow through licensed and approved investment funds. The ministry also highlighted three channels for registering labour complaints related to domestic workers when disputes between workers and employers cannot be settled amicably. Complaints can be filed through the MOHRE UAE app, the ministry’s website or by contacting the Labour Claims and Consultation Centre on 80084. The ministry also outlined the benefits of the optional savings system, under which amounts allocated for the end-of-service gratuity of employees working in private sector companies are invested in leading investment funds approved by the Securities and Commodities Authority, allowing employees’ savings to grow through investment returns. It said the savings system aims to support the UAE’s economic system, enhance the protection and well-being of the country’s workforce, increase individual investment returns for beneficiaries and allow workers to make additional optional contributions. The system also aims to enhance the attractiveness and flexibility of the labour market by improving services provided to workers, while taking advantage of opportunities to invest funds in investment instruments for economic activities in the country.

headline: PNP to work with foreign counterparts in Thomas Markle probe
snippet: THE Philippine National Police (PNP) will work with law enforcement agencies abroad in looking into allegations linking the father of Meghan Markle, the duchess of Sussex, to the possession of child abuse and exploitation images. Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., PNP chief, emphasized the need for cross-border cooperation in investigating Thomas Markle, particularly the cases that may involve digital evidence and individuals with links to different countries. “The safety of our children remains a priority. Those who try to engage in child exploitation often extend beyond borders, and as such, it emphasizes the importance of strong coordination with our foreign counterparts,” Nartatez said. Authorities said the elder Markle possessed images of child abuse reportedly found among his belongings at his former home in Cebu. He reportedly has denied the allegations. Digital forensics on a laptop in the Markle house is being conducted and full results are expected to be released next week, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said. Nartatez said the PNP maintains a zero-tolerance policy against child exploitation and is committed to protecting minors from abuse, including forms of exploitation facilitated by digital platforms and cross-border networks. Markle, whose daughter is married to Britain's Prince Harry, had been living in Cebu until reportedly returning to the United States earlier this year. The British tabloid the Sun first reported last week that Markle's son, Thomas Markle Jr., had discovered the child abuse images while going through boxes found in his father's former home. On Friday, Meghan Markle said she was "deeply distressed" by accusations her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous "troubling and disturbing" allegations. After the reports, Meghan said that in 2018 she had seen a letter sent to London's Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection making similar accusations. "It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father, and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," she said in a statement. London's Metropolitan police said it had passed on the information to the royal couple but did not share it with other law enforcement agencies. snippet: The Halloween horror movie is the title I’m most excited to stream this week. Now that Halloween is finally here, it’s time to trot out all the favorites of Spooky Season. Last week, I was most excited to stream “Sleepy Hollow,” and I can confirm after going through with that rewatch that the film will be on my Halloween lead-up watchlist again next year. A more recent addition to that list is “Trick 'r Treat,” the 2007 film that served as Michael Dougherty’s directorial debut. It’s definitely more horror-focused than “Sleepy Hollow,” but this is the perfect time of year for the movie, and it’s the title I’m most excited to stream this week. “Trick ‘r Treat” tells four Halloween stories with a common thread running through them: Sam, a small demon wearing a threadbare costume and a burlap sack for a mask, to punish those who disrespect the traditions of the holiday. Refuse to keep your jack-o’-lantern lit? No candy for the trick-or-treaters? You can expect a visit from Sam, and the end result will be far from sweet. While there are a ton of horror movies set around Halloween, I always liked “Trick ‘r Treat” because of the base premise of the film: Halloween is a true holiday to be revered, and if one disrespects it, there will be consequences. Sam is like the Krampus of Halloween, and he metes out judgment with glee. It’s something of an anthology movie, and viewers will see a few big-name actors sprinkled throughout, including Brian Cox and Anna Paquin. Cox especially stands out as Mr. Kreeg, the curmudgeonly Halloween hater who is confused to be spared from the carnage once he inadvertently carries out a Halloween tradition by giving Sam a few treats. Keep in mind if you’re going to turn this one on during the lead-up to Halloween, it’s not for kids. “Trick ‘r Treat” is rated R, with plenty of violence and language, and even some nudity. Keep it well away from the young ones, and make sure it’s over by the time they’re back from their own trick-or-treat run. “Trick ‘r Treat” isn’t the best horror movie under the sun, but it takes an original concept and parlays it into some gory Halloween fun. That’s what I’m looking for this time of year, and it’s the title I’m most excited to watch this week. According to the International Weightlifting Federation, athletes must compete in a minimum of five of the 10 qualifying competitions to earn a ranking for the 2028 Olympics. The calendar is split into two periods, with Period One consisting of six events and three totals needed, and Period Two consisting of four events and two totals needed. headline: Russian Tourists Skip Crowded Sochi for Fiji and Madagascar as Prices Parity Hits
snippet: On the coastal highway between Juba and Sochi, traffic has ground to a halt, a familiar sight for domestic tourists during peak season. Yet, in an airport lounge in Moscow, a family is comparing the cost of a week in the Caucasus with a package to the Indian Ocean islands. The math, they find, no longer favors the domestic resort. This shift marks a tangible break in the Russian tourism market: a segment of budget-conscious travelers is bypassing crowded southern regions in favor of long-haul destinations like Fiji and Madagascar, driven by a convergence of rising local prices and competitive international airfares. According to data from the telecommunications company MegaFon, this is not a fleeting trend but a structural change in booking behavior. While domestic tourist traffic grew by a modest 4.3%, demand for remote international destinations surged. Fiji recorded a 147% increase in subscribers, while Madagascar saw Russian tourist numbers rise by 2.6 times. Cabo Verde and Jamaica also posted significant growth of 79% and 61%, respectively. This data suggests a reallocation of spending rather than a simple increase in travel volume. The Price Parity Point The driving force behind this shift is economic. For a family, a one-week holiday in a quality hotel in Sirius or Krasnaya Polyana now costs between 250,000 and 300,000 rubles, inclusive of flights, transfers, and on-site expenses. This price point has become comparable to package tours to Africa or Oceania. Ilya Rodenko, a tourism market analyst, told Pravda. Ru that the middle class is increasingly reluctant to overpay for overloaded infrastructure in southern Russia. When travelers compare the final bill for a domestic trip with the cost of an exotic island getaway, they often find that the latter offers a higher quality of rest and more unique experiences for a similar investment.

Archbishop scrambles to wash his hands of Trump after laying them on him: report
snippet: The Denver archbishop who led a prayer over President Donald Trump in the Oval Office is now scrambling to explain himself. Archbishop James Golka told the Denver Catholic, the archdiocese's own newspaper, on Friday that the White House's video of the Oct. 22 prayer was never meant as an endorsement, even as he defended being there and turned his fire on critics. "I understand that many people saw the video, posted by the Administration twelve days before an election, as an endorsement," Golka said. "That was never my intention." The invitation came months ago, according to the archbishop, following a June session in which faith leaders pressed the administration on immigration, religious freedom and visas for religious workers. He said progress made by task forces after that meeting encouraged him to accept, even though he knew the meeting "could be shared and some might use it for political purposes." Golka said he learned only shortly before the visit that he would be the one praying over Trump. The bishops first spent three hours with the White House Faith Office discussing religious worker visas, protection of life, religious freedom and school choice. "I've had a lot of people, really good friends, ask me, 'What were you doing?' 'Why did you do that?' I just answer, 'I was being a Catholic priest,'" he said. The archbishop then pointed outward. "I'm heartbroken that people are hurt, and that there are people intentionally using this moment to sow disunity. That's not a fruit of the Spirit," he said, urging Catholics to look past headlines he described as "often crafted to provoke." The fallout has reached Rome. Catholic commentator Christopher Hale reported in his Letters from Leo newsletter that a senior official at the Vatican's Dicastery for Bishops called it "a highly inappropriate meeting and insult to Pope Leo." Hale wrote that Golka's account stops short of an apology and never mentions Paula White-Cain, the televangelist and White House Faith Office adviser who stood behind Trump's chair as the bishops laid hands on him. The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops has said it neither organized the meeting nor has any affiliation with it. Golka closed with a pledge. "This work helps only if the Church carries the same message to leaders of both parties. We will," he said.
